The story follows a clear, logical progression that creates a deeply unified and atmospheric whole. Beginning at the threshold as Miriam unlocks the front door, the narrative moves naturally through the hallway and into the kitchen. Every sensory detail—the muscle memory of lifting the door, the silence, the untouched blue coat, the worn banister, and the dried coffee in the espresso maker—serves the central theme of grief, absence, and the passage of time. There are no disjointed or unnecessary elements; each observation and small action builds upon the last, culminating in a quiet, resonant ending where Miriam is left confronting the reality of what has been left behind.
